description: Seed-library refresh (83-band). The 245 seed notebooks across 14 domains are the product's foundation and worked examples, and today their upkeep is owned by nothing: no process detects rot (a Resources URL that has died, a code cell that no longer compiles under a current interpreter), no policy governs refreshing a stale seed, no path promotes the docs/explanation/gap-analysis.md §2 recommended additions into the library, and no policy governs adding a domain (the numbering runs 01–15 with 06 a permanent hole). This band adds all four as maintenance machinery over the SHIPPED graders and constructor — never a parallel one. The idempotence invariants in CLAUDE.md are the hard constraints: the seed library is held to gate_failures (not construction_failures) so it stays green; an already-✅ notebook is SKIPPED, NEVER REWRITTEN, unless force=True; content that fails the grader is never written; and notebooks/ ships with the app and is never written to at runtime — so a refresh is a REPO-MAINTENANCE operation (an audited, committed change), not an in-app write. Rot findings therefore split into exactly two outcomes: FLAGGED-FOR-HUMAN (the default — a report names the notebook, the dead URL / failing cell, and the grader sentence) or FORCE-REGENERATE (an explicit, per-notebook, opt-in force=True pass through the shipped construct_topic, graded before write like any construction). No third path silently rewrites a ✅ seed. Anti-fabrication: the audit only reports what it measured (a real HTTP liveness result per URL, a real compile() result per code cell); a refreshed notebook is written only when the shipped grader passes; the promotion path drives §2 topics through the real construct → gate pipeline rather than marking them done.
warmup: echo '--- the two graders: seeds are held to gate_failures; construction_failures adds the URL + compile() checks the audit reuses ---'; grep -n 'def gate_failures\|def construction_failures\|https\|compile' praxis/rubric.py | head
echo '--- the idempotence invariants a refresh must respect ---'; grep -n 'force\|skipped\|never' praxis/construct.py | head
echo '--- the corpus: 245 seeds, 14 domains, 06 is a hole ---'; ls notebooks/; echo "total: $(find notebooks -name '*.ipynb' | wc -l)"
echo '--- the promotion backlog: recommended-tagged topics from docs/explanation/gap-analysis.md section 2 ---'; grep -n 'recommended' curriculum.py | head

userStories.title: Rot audit: URL liveness + compile() re-check over the 245 seeds, report-only
acceptanceCriteria: An audit pass sweeps every seed notebook checking (a) each https:// URL under Resources for liveness (a real HTTP request with a sane timeout; a network-unavailable run reports 'unchecked', never 'live') and (b) each code cell against compile() under the current interpreter — reusing the same checks construction_failures already implements rather than a parallel grader — plus a gate_failures re-check so a seed that has drifted below the shipped bar is caught.

The audit is strictly read-only: it never writes or rewrites a notebook (the seed library stays held to gate_failures and stays green), and its output is a machine-readable report naming each rotted notebook, the specific dead URL or failing cell, and the grader's own sentence for it.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that the audit flags a fixture notebook with a dead URL and one with a non-compiling cell (against a stubbed HTTP layer — no live network in tests) and passes a healthy one.
userStories.notes: Added read-only praxis.audit JSON/CLI sweep using construction_failures, gate_failures, and compile checks; fixture tests cover dead URL, syntax failure, healthy, offline unchecked, and byte-identical input. Full pytest: 911 passed, 1 skipped.

userStories.title: Refresh policy: flagged-for-human by default, force-regenerate only explicitly
acceptanceCriteria: A documented refresh policy (docs/) turns audit findings into exactly two outcomes: FLAGGED-FOR-HUMAN (the default — the report is the deliverable, a maintainer decides) or FORCE-REGENERATE (an explicit, per-notebook opt-in that runs the shipped construct_topic with force=True, so the result is graded by construction_failures before anything is written) — there is no path that silently rewrites a ✅ seed, preserving the skip-if-✅ idempotence invariant for everything not explicitly forced.

A refresh is a repo-maintenance operation, not an in-app write: notebooks/ ships with the app and is never written at runtime, so the regenerate path runs from the repo (CLI/maintenance entry point) and its output lands as a reviewable diff; a regeneration whose result fails the grader writes nothing and leaves the existing seed in place.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that a flagged notebook is untouched by default, that force-regenerating a fixture notebook goes through the shipped grader (a failing regeneration leaves the original byte-identical), and that an un-flagged ✅ notebook is never a regeneration target.
userStories.notes: Added documented FLAGGED-FOR-HUMAN / FORCE-REGENERATE policy and repo-only praxis.refresh CLI/API; forced candidates delegate to construct_path with force=True and the shipped construction grader writes only passing content. Full pytest: 914 passed, 1 skipped; refresh tests: 6 passed.

userStories.title: Promotion path for gap-analysis §2 additions + a domain-addition policy (the 06 hole)
acceptanceCriteria: A promotion path turns docs/explanation/gap-analysis.md §2 recommended additions (already scaffolded and tagged recommended in curriculum.py) into full seed-library members by driving them through the SHIPPED pipeline — construct to ✅ via construct_topic, gate via checks.py — and records the promotion in docs/explanation/gap-analysis.md (the entry moves from §2 backlog to §1 coverage); a promoted topic is never hand-marked done without a passing grade.

A domain-addition policy is documented in docs/: the numbering runs 01–15 with 06 a permanent hole — a new domain APPENDS the next free number (16+), never reuses 06 — and adding a domain means a Domain entry in curriculum.py's DOMAINS, a notebooks/NN-slug directory, and a gap-analysis coverage section; a test asserts the on-disk domain directories, the DOMAINS list, and the no-reuse-of-06 rule agree.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including the domain-numbering consistency test and a test that the promotion path refuses to record a promotion for a topic whose notebook is not ✅ or whose checkset is absent.
userStories.notes: Added praxis.promote repository path: construct_topic with checks=True, gate_failures, and checkset_failures must all pass before moving a recommended entry from gap-analysis §2 to §1. Added domain-addition policy and manifest/directory validator reserving 06. Full pytest: 917 passed, 1 skipped; promotion tests: 6 passed.
